experiments.description: RAG Studio's default pipeline answered by claude-haiku-5-5 and judged by claude-haiku-5-5 — the reference run every paid sweep shares.
experiments.hypothesis: Reference run for H2′–H6; no claim of its own.
experiments.name: baseline

experiments.description: RAG Studio RQ4 restated with claude-haiku-5-5 — how chunk size affects retrieval and answers.
experiments.hypothesis: H4: Chunk size 1000 has hit@8 at least 5 points above chunk size 4000 (finer chunks rank evidence higher), while chunk size 4000 has an answer rate at least 5 points above chunk size 1000 (more context per chunk). H4 is rejected if either gap is under 5 points or has the opposite sign. (Run here with claude-haiku-5-5 answering instead of claude-sonnet-5-5.)
experiments.name: chunk-sweep

experiments.description: RAG Studio RQ2 restated, reduced to three thresholds to fit the budget — the relevance gate's answer-rate vs refusal trade-off.
experiments.hypothesis: H2′ (H2 from rag-studio commit 8c829e1, sweep reduced from 0.20–0.60 in nine steps to 0.25/0.35/0.45 for budget): raising min_similarity from 0.25 to 0.45 does not raise the answer rate on answerable questions and does raise refusal recall on unanswerable questions; some threshold in the sweep reaches an answer rate of at least 80% and refusal recall of at least 70% together. H2′ is rejected if any clause fails.
experiments.name: gate-sweep

experiments.description: EXPLORATORY (not pre-registered) — written after gate-sweep showed every question's best match scores 0.60–0.82, so thresholds of 0.25–0.45 never gate. Tests whether the similarity gate can separate answerable from unanswerable questions on this corpus at all.
experiments.hypothesis: Exploratory question, written after seeing the max-similarity distribution: does any threshold between 0.65 and 0.80 raise refusal of unanswerable questions without blocking answerable ones? No pass/fail claim.
experiments.name: gate-sweep-high

experiments.description: Checks the regression gate itself — a plausible "make it cheaper" change (fewer, bigger chunks) must be flagged.
experiments.hypothesis: The gate flags the aggressive config: comparing baseline to aggressive shows at least one regressed case and a negative hit@k delta, and `evallab compare --gate` exits non-zero.
experiments.name: gate-validation

experiments.description: Is claude-haiku-5-5 good enough for grounded, abstaining answers? Same pipeline, judge and dataset; only the answering model changes.
experiments.hypothesis: H5: claude-haiku-5-5 accuracy is within 5 points of claude-sonnet-5-5 at no more than 10% of the system cost per case. H5 is rejected if haiku's accuracy is more than 5 points below sonnet's, or its cost per case is above 10% of sonnet's.
experiments.name: model-sweep

experiments.description: Calibration only — measures real tokens and cost per case (including thinking) for each model before any sweep.
experiments.hypothesis: Calibration only: measures tokens per case; no claim.
experiments.name: probe

experiments.description: Does asking for terse, fully cited answers reduce unsupported claims?
experiments.hypothesis: H6: With prompt_variant terse_cite_all, the share of answered cases the judge finds at least one unsupported claim in is at least 5 points lower than with the default prompt, and the answer rate on answerable questions is not more than 5 points lower. H6 is rejected if either clause fails.
experiments.name: prompt-sweep

experiments.description: Exploratory — how chunk size and top_k move retrieval (hit@k, MRR) on hybrid retrieval. No hypothesis; no API calls.
experiments.name: retrieval-sweep

experiments.description: RAG Studio RQ1 restated — does hybrid retrieval beat vector-only and BM25-only? Retrieval only, no API calls.
experiments.hypothesis: H1: On `exact_term` questions, hybrid hit@8 is at least 10 points above vector-only hit@8. On `natural` questions, hybrid hit@8 is within 5 points of vector-only hit@8 (not lower by more than 5). Overall, hybrid hit@8 is at least as high as the better of the two single modes. H1 is rejected if hybrid's `exact_term` gain over vector is under 10 points, or if hybrid is more than 5 points below vector on `natural`.
experiments.name: rq1-retrieval

experiments.description: RAG Studio RQ3 restated — does server-side citation verification remove unsupported claims prompting lets through?
experiments.hypothesis: H3′ (H3 from rag-studio commit 8c829e1, measured per answer because this judge counts unsupported claims per answer): raw citation validity with verification off is below 98%, and the share of answered cases with at least one unsupported claim is at least 3 points lower with verification on than off. H3′ is rejected if raw citation validity is 98% or higher, or the share does not fall by 3 points.
experiments.name: verify-ablation
